items.howItWorks: Relieves pain and inflammation on the affected area
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for the analgesic and anti-inflammatory relief of bruises, shoulder stiffness, and rheumatic pain.
items.usage:
Clean and dry the affected area, then attach 1 sheet once a day, 1 time a day.

Fix it with a bandage, adhesive plaster, etc. as needed.
items.precaution:
Do not use this medicine on eczema, dermatitis caused by lacquer, etc., or wounded areas.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have experienced allergic symptoms (e.g., rash, redness, itching, dermatitis caused by lacquer, etc.) due to medicines or cosmetics, have an allergic constitution, are a patient with severe dampness or soreness, are pregnant or possibly pregnant, or are breastfeeding.

Strictly observe the prescribed dosage and administration.

When administering to children, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

If there is no improvement in symptoms after using for 5 to 6 days, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Since toxic symptoms may appear if a large amount is absorbed through the skin, avoid long-term use over a wide surface.

For external use only.
items.adverse: If rash, redness (congestion and reddening), itching, etc. appear due to the use of this medicine, stop use and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

items.howItWorks: Relieves joint and muscle pain and inflammation topically
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for the analgesic and anti-inflammatory (anti-inflammation) relief of degenerative arthritis (osteoarthritis), periarthritis of the shoulder, tendon and tenosynovitis (synovitis of the tendon sheath), epicondylitis of the humerus (upper arm bone) (tennis elbow, etc.), muscle pain, and swelling (edema) and pain (aching) after trauma (wounds).
items.usage: Peel off the release paper of the medicated surface and attach to the affected area twice a day. Wipe off sweat from the application area before use.
items.precaution: Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, or patients with or those who have experienced aspirin asthma (induction of asthma attacks by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, etc.) must not use this medicine. Before using this medicine, patients with bronchial asthma, women who are pregnant or possibly pregnant, children, the elderly, inflammation accompanied by infection, and those with chronic diseases should consult a doctor or pharmacist. Do not use on damaged skin and mucous membranes, or on areas with eczema or rash. Wipe off sweat from the application area before use.
items.adverse: If redness (congestion and reddening), rash, drug eruption (drug rash), itching and burning sensation, contact dermatitis, asthma attack (dry rales (bubbling sounds), wheezing (wheezing breathing), difficulty breathing, etc.), etc. occasionally appear, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

items.howItWorks: Prevents infection and eases pain from wounds and burns
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for the prevention of infection and relief of pain due to cuts, wounds, and burns.
items.usage: For those 2 years and older, apply an appropriate amount to the affected area 1 to 3 times a day.
items.precaution: Patients with hypersensitivity to aminoglycoside antibiotics and bacitracin, and patients with a perforated (punctured) eardrum must not use this medicine. For external use only. Do not use for ophthalmic purposes. If there is no improvement in symptoms after using for 2 weeks or more, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
items.adverse: If rash, itching, redness (congestion and reddening), swelling (edema), papules, small blisters (vesicles), overgrowth of resistant or non-susceptible bacteria, irritation, hypersensitivity reactions, etc. appear, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

items.efficacy: This medicine is used for dermatophytosis (tinea (tinea manuum, tinea pedis, tinea cruris), cutaneous candidiasis, tinea versicolor) and erythrasma.
items.usage: Before applying, wash the affected area clean, then apply to the affected area twice a day. In particular, wash the areas between the fingers and toes clean, then dry completely before applying this medicine. Continue treatment for 2 to 3 weeks, and for severe infections (especially in the case of infection between the hands or toes) continue for up to 4 weeks, and to prevent recurrence continue treatment for at least about 2 more weeks after treatment. For the treatment of athlete's foot on the hands or toes, it is advisable to apply this medicine to clean gauze and cover the infected area.
items.precaution: Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or imidazole derivatives, patients with peculiar skin diseases, and areas with severe erosion (soreness) must not use this medicine. Before using this medicine, women who are pregnant or possibly pregnant and breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist. Do not use the occlusive dressing method or wrapping method unless directed by a doctor. In the case of candidiasis, do not use acidic soap. Since the oleaginous ingredient used as the base of this medicine may degrade or damage the quality of contraceptive latex rubber products such as condoms, be careful to avoid contact as much as possible. Apply this medicine for external use only. When applying to the facial area, be careful to avoid contact with the eyes.
items.adverse: Allergic skin reactions, erythema (red spots) at the application site, pain, blister formation, commonly irritation and burning sensation at the application site, occasionally moist eczema, sweating, contact dermatitis, dryness at the application site, itching, and rarely swelling, cracks, etc. at the application site may appear.

items.howItWorks: Soothes allergic skin inflammation and itching topically
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for allergic dermatitis, cosmetic poisoning, prickly heat, itching, contact dermatitis (diaper rash), shaving irritation, and prevention of rough skin.
items.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area several times a day, or apply it soaked into gauze, etc.
items.precaution: Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine; skin infections (tuberculosis, syphilis, candidiasis, athlete's foot, tinea, herpes zoster, herpes simplex, chickenpox, vaccinia, scabies, pubic lice); suppuration (festering); otitis externa of the ear canal with eczema and eardrum perforation; ulcers (excluding Behcet's disease); burns and frostbite of second-degree deep type (not exposed) or worse; perioral dermatitis; acne vulgaris; rosacea patients; and wounds or mucous membrane areas must not use this medicine. Before using this medicine, those with an allergic constitution, women who are pregnant or possibly pregnant and breastfeeding women, infants and children, patients with extensive affected areas, and patients with or those who have experienced hypersensitivity to propylene glycol should consult a doctor or pharmacist. Strictly observe the prescribed dosage and administration. When administering to children, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Use this medicine for external use only and do not use internally. be careful to avoid getting it in the eyes, and if it gets in the eyes, immediately rinse out with water. Do not use for purposes other than treatment, such as after makeup or shaving. Do not use the occlusive dressing method without a doctor's supervision.
items.adverse: If impetigo contagiosa (pus-crust disease), folliculitis, viral infections, boils, skin irritation, stinging pain (pricking-like pain), fever, persistent irritation, rash, redness (congestion and reddening), flushing, itching, dry skin, pustular (pus-blister) dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, prickly heat, wound aggravation, bedsores, pustulosis (pus-blister condition), athlete's foot, tinea and other dermatophytosis, acne, suppuration (festering), etc. appear, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. When used on the eyelid skin, increased intraocular pressure, glaucoma (blurred vision), etc. may appear.

items.howItWorks: Softens and treats scars and skin injuries topically
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for hypertrophic and keloidal, movement-restricting or cosmetically disfiguring wounds and scars from surgery, amputation, burns, and accidents; traumatic contractures; and cicatricial strictures.
items.usage: Massage gently several times a day until it sufficiently penetrates the wound area. If the wound is severe or an old scar, fix it with a dressing and leave it overnight.
items.precaution: Patients with hypersensitivity to methyl parahydroxybenzoate and this medicine, pregnant women, and patients with incised or unhealed wounds or with oozing wound areas on the mucous membrane skin must not use this medicine. Before using this medicine, breastfeeding women, patients with hypersensitivity to propylene glycol, and those who have experienced allergies should consult a doctor or pharmacist. When administering to children, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. be careful to prevent the wound from being exposed to solar heat or light, and in the case of a fresh wound, avoid physical stimulation such as extreme cold, ultraviolet rays, or strong massage.
items.adverse: Very rarely, local skin irritation (e.g., itching, hypersensitivity reactions), etc. may appear.

items.efficacy: This medicine is used for dermatophytosis of tinea (tinea corporis, tinea cruris, tinea pedis), cutaneous candidiasis, tinea versicolor, and seborrheic dermatitis.
items.usage: Usually apply once a day, or twice a day depending on the severity of the infection. Continue applying for several days even after symptoms have disappeared.
items.precaution: Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, and areas of the scalp with wounds or inflammation and areas with severe erosion (soreness) must not use this medicine. Before using this medicine, women who are pregnant or possibly pregnant and breastfeeding women, children, and patients with or those who have experienced hypersensitivity to propylene glycol should consult a doctor or pharmacist. In the case of candidiasis, do not use acidic soap. Do not use the occlusive dressing method or wrapping method unless directed by a doctor. Use this medicine for external use only. Do not use this medicine for ophthalmic purposes; apply taking care to avoid contact with the eyes, and if it accidentally gets in the eyes, rinse out completely with a sufficient amount of water.
items.adverse: At the application site, occasionally contact dermatitis, rash, skin burning sensation, skin peeling, blister rash, sticky skin, hypersensitivity, erythema, itching, dryness, irritation, bleeding, discomfort, inflammation, paresthesia, and very rarely urticaria, pain, burns, etc. may appear.
items.interaction: When used together with antifungal agents of the same kind (miconazole, econazole, isoconazole, etc.), consult a doctor or pharmacist.

items.howItWorks: Prevents motion-sickness nausea via a behind-the-ear patch
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for the prevention of nausea and vomiting due to motion sickness.
items.usage: Adults attach 1 patch (1.5 mg as scopolamine) per use to the surface of dry, hairless skin behind the ear at least 4 hours in advance. One patch has an effect lasting for 3 days, and if it needs to be applied for more than 3 days, the first one should be removed and another patch attached behind the ear on the opposite side to the one where it was attached.
items.precaution: Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or the ointment base, narrow-angle glaucoma, bradycardia, urination disorders such as prostatic hypertrophy, pregnant women, breastfeeding women, and infants and young children 7 years of age or younger must not use this medicine. Before using this medicine, the elderly, and patients with metabolic disease, liver disease, kidney disease, pyloric stenosis, bladder obstruction, intestinal obstruction, seizures or mental illness should consult a doctor or pharmacist. Since drowsiness, disorientation, confusion, etc. may appear after using this medicine, be careful when driving and operating machinery. Since there is irritation if a hand smeared with the medicine touches mucous membranes such as the eyes, immediately wash your hands well with soap after touching this medicine.
items.adverse: If confusion, anxiety, hallucinations, delusions, or symptoms of acute narrow-angle glaucoma (eye pain and congestion accompanied by pupil dilation) appear, remove this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist. If dry mouth occasionally, temporary blurred vision, visual disturbances such as pupil dilation, and rarely dry eyes, itching, flushing, tachycardia, increased viscosity of bronchial secretions, urination disorders, rash, erythema, drowsiness, disorientation, memory impairment, dizziness, anxiety, hallucinations, confusion, etc. appear, consult a doctor or pharmacist. After stopping use of this medicine, withdrawal symptoms (dizziness, nausea, vomiting, headache, balance disturbance) may appear.
items.interaction: When used together with central nervous system-acting drugs such as alcohol, especially anticholinergic drugs (belladonna alkaloid preparations), antihistamines, antidepressants, and H2-receptor blockers, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
